## 1 · Cleaning messy data

| Look at | Fix with |
|---|---|
| `names()` | `janitor::clean_names()` |
| `count(d, sex)` for every category | `case_when()`, `str_trim()`, `str_to_lower()`, `fct_recode()` |
| `glimpse()`: text in a number column | `parse_number("7.2 g")`; first list what becomes `NA` |
| Dates in two formats | `coalesce(ymd(x, quiet = TRUE), dmy(x, quiet = TRUE))` |
| Placeholders (999), impossible values | `na_if(age, 999)`, `if_else(sbp > 300, NA, sbp)`: set to `NA`, keep the row |
| Duplicates | `distinct()` for exact copies; `get_dupes(id)` and **check the forms** |

Never edit the raw file. Count every change and keep a **cleaning log** for the methods.

## 2 · Iteration

| Need | Code |
|---|---|
| Same step on many columns | `summarise(across(c(sbp, dbp), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)))` |
| Columns by type | `across(where(is.numeric), ...)` |
| Loop over names | `for (v in vars) print(mean(d[[v]], na.rm = TRUE))` |
| One result per item | `sapply(d[vars], mean, na.rm = TRUE)`, `map_dbl()`, `map_dfr()` |
| Formula from text | `reformulate("sex", "sbp")` gives `sbp ~ sex` |
| Your own function | `f <- function(x, cut) mean(x >= cut, na.rm = TRUE)`; test it on a known case |

`d$v` looks for a column called "v"; use `d[[v]]`. Many tests → many p-values: adjust or pre-specify.

## 3 · Plot design and ggplot2

| Goal | Chart |
|---|---|
| Distribution | histogram, density, box, violin, ridgeline |
| Correlation | scatter (+ `geom_smooth()`), hexbin when points overlap |
| Ranking | sorted horizontal bars, dot or lollipop |
| Part of whole | stacked bar; pie only for ≤ 5 categories |
| Evolution | line (ordered x), with a band for uncertainty |
| Flow | Sankey / alluvial |

| ggplot2 | Rule |
|---|---|
| `aes(colour = sex)` | **inside** `aes()` = mapped to data; `geom_point(colour = "blue")` = fixed |
| `facet_wrap(~ region)` / `facet_grid(sex ~ region)` | one variable wrapped / rows × columns; `scales = "free_y"` loses comparability |
| `geom_col()` / `geom_bar()` | heights given / rows counted; bars **start at 0** |
| `geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)))` | puts a density curve on the same scale |
| `theme_minimal()`, `theme_void()` | report / map |

Grey most data, colour the message; colour-blind-safe palettes (`scale_colour_viridis_d()`); no 3D, no dual axes.

## 4 · Table 1 (gtsummary) and ggstatsplot

```
d |> select(age, sex, bmi, htn) |>
  tbl_summary(by = htn, statistic = list(all_continuous() ~ "{median} ({p25}, {p75})",
                                         all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)")) |>
  add_overall() |> add_p() |> bold_labels()
tbl_regression(glm(y ~ x, family = binomial), exponentiate = TRUE)   # odds ratios
```

**Randomised trial: no baseline p-values.** Report missing counts and the n analysed. Word: `as_flex_table()`.

| ggstatsplot | Use |
|---|---|
| `ggbetweenstats()` / `ggwithinstats(subject.id = id)` | groups / same people measured again |
| `ggbarstats()`, `ggpiestats()` | proportions |
| `type = "bayes"` | prints log(BF01); BF01 = exp(value), > 3 favours no difference |

## 5 · Tests in context

| Data | Test | R |
|---|---|---|
| One categorical vs expected proportions | goodness-of-fit | `chisq.test(x = tab, p = c(0.5, 0.5))` |
| Two categorical, independent people | chi-square | `chisq.test(table(a, b))` |
| Yes/no **before and after**, same people | McNemar | `mcnemar.test(table(before, after))` |
| Is it roughly normal? | Q-Q plot | `qqnorm(x); qqline(x)` (look at the tails) |

## 6 · Reports and export

| Need | Write |
|---|---|
| A parameter | YAML `params: region: "North"`, code `params$region` |
| Render one report per site | `quarto render report.qmd -P region:South` |
| Citable figure / table | `#| label: fig-bp` / `tbl-base`, then `@fig-bp` |
| PDF output | needs LaTeX: `tinytex::install_tinytex()` |
| Save a ggplot | `ggsave("f.png", p, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)`; `.pdf` / `.svg` for vector |
| Base graphics | `png("f.png"); plot(x); dev.off()` |

300 dpi for print, 72–150 for screen. Interactive: `plotly::ggplotly(p)`.
